visual_audit_fix_final_2026-08-21.note: Final sign-off pass. Three findings, two of them MAJOR regressions introduced by the round-2 fixes (the widened .c10-pane-index narrowed the right pane; the new 760 KEY SETTINGS stack exposed a long-standing specificity bug). fixes.f1_domain_overview_count_never_clipped: MAJOR / regression. In the glass themes at 1280 the right-pane SECTIONS count for 'Accounts & Sign-in' rendered as '4' while the same screen's middle column said '44'. Cause: .c10-mgr-row was grid-template-columns 20px 1fr auto 14px, and .c10-item-meta carries overflow:hidden, which zeroes its automatic minimum size — so the nowrap description in the 1fr track claimed everything and collapsed the count cell to one glyph, with no ellipsis to warn the reader. Fix: (a) the text track is now minmax(0, 1fr) so the DESCRIPTION is what yields; (b) the wrapper span gained a class, .c10-mgr-text { min-width: 0 }, so its content can actually shrink (JS: both .c10-mgr-row emitters in catOverviewPane); (c) .c10-mgr-row > .c10-item-meta and > .c10-word now set min-width:max-content, max-width:none, overflow:visible, text-overflow:clip — a count or status word cannot be squeezed at all, in any theme at any width; (d) .c10-mgr-title gained display:block + ellipsis so a long section title truncates honestly instead of overflowing. Measured (live getBoundingClientRect, file:// CDP): glass-dark-1280 and glass-light-1280 'Accounts & Sign-in' meta width 5.58px vs scrollWidth 16px (CLIPPED) -> 12.73px vs scrollWidth 13px (NOT clipped); 40 and 28 unchanged at 12.73px. Description now ellipsizes with a visible '…' instead. friendly-dark-1280 unchanged (11.13px, never clipped, description still fits in full). Verified visually at 2x on glass-dark-1280, glass-light-1280, friendly-dark-1280 and glass-dark-900: 44 + 40 + 28 = 112, matching the pane's own '112 settings'.
fixes.f2_f3_narrow_row_rhythm_binds_value_to_i: MAJOR / regression, covering findings 2 (basic-dark 760) and 3 (glass-light 760) — one defect, all eight themes. At one-pane width .c10-row stacks the value UNDER its own name, so vertical rhythm is the only cue for which value belongs to which setting; measured gaps were 10px INSIDE a row and 0px BETWEEN rows, so every value read as the value of the NEXT setting ('Default Model: Not set' when Default Model is Claude Opus 4). Root cause is a CSS specificity trap, not the round-2 layout: `.c10 button` (0,1,1) out-specifies the authored `.c10-row { padding: 5px 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid }` (0,1,0), so rows shipped with computed padding 0px and border-bottom-width 0px while the 10px grid `gap` still applied between the two stacked lines. Fix (scoped to one-pane width so the wide table is untouched): .c10.is-mode1 .c10-row now sets row-gap:2px, padding:7px 10px 8px and border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-light) at a winning specificity (0,3,0), with .c10.is-mode1 .c10-rows > .c10-row:last-child dropping the trailing hairline. The state word also moved from grid-row 1/span 2 to grid-row 1 (align-self:center) so 'Reconnect' / '—' sits on its setting's NAME line instead of floating in the gutter between name and value. Measured after (live boxes at 760): intra-row name->value gap 2.5px, inter-row value->next-name gap 16.5px — a 6.6:1 ratio in the correct direction, replacing the previous 10px-vs-0px inversion. Identical in basic-dark, friendly-dark and glass-light at 760, and at 900 (also one-pane). The same rhythm now applies to the full rows pane at 760, not just the KEY SETTINGS block: dest/ai/accounts measures 2.5px vs 16.5px on every row.

visual_audit_fix_round4_2026-08-21.note: Full-coverage sweep (112 screenshots) round. Four MAJOR layout findings, all fixed. Findings 2, 3 and 4 turned out to share ONE root cause with the round-3 finding-2 defect and are fixed at source this time rather than patched per-surface: the button reset at the top of the stylesheet was authored as `.c10 button` (0,1,1) and out-specified every single-class rule on the concept's interactive surfaces (0,1,0). It is now wrapped as `:where(.c10 button)` (0,0,0). Also confirmed the three central _shared2/pm2-tokens.css fixes named in the brief and deliberately NOT re-done here (that file is not owned by this concept): retro-light --accent-lime #1B6E34 (pm2-tokens.css line 83, and retro maps --accent-primary onto it, so it is the colour of every t-setup/t-progress status word and every Back control on that face), glass-light --accent-warning #6E4700 / --accent-orange #6E3B00 (lines 72-73), glass-dark --text-muted rgba(237,231,248,0.72) (line 89). Verified by eye at 2x on retro-light-1280-manager (Not signed in / Refreshing / Signed in, cannot invoke / Ready all legible on cream) and glass-light-1280-dest-ai + glass-light-760-dest-ai (Reconnect state cell and the 44/40/28 counts legible on the lilac mesh).
visual_audit_fix_round4_2026-08-21.root_cause: `.c10 button { padding:0; border:none; background:none; color:inherit; text-align:left }` was (0,1,1). Nearly every surface in this concept IS a <button> with one class: .c10-item, .c10-mgr-row, .c10-row, .c10-att-row, .c10-recent-row, .c10-vrow, .c10-ix-item, .c10-btn, .c10-util, .c10-res, .c10-check, .c10-src, .c10-tab, .c10-facet-check, .c10-opt, .c10-more, .c10-advbar, .c10-ro-top, .c10-citem-top, .c10-catpick, .c10-countchip, .c10-crumb, .c10-back, .c10-close, .c10-editor-close, .c10-detail-toggle, .c10-qa-jump. Every one of those rules is (0,1,0), so the reset beat all of them; only :hover / .is-active rules (0,2,0) ever won, which is why hover backgrounds appeared while the padding they were drawn for did not. Census taken live (getComputedStyle over every .c10 button on 10 routes x 760/1280/2200, file:// CDP): 26 of 27 distinct button classes computed padding 0px 0px 0px 0px and border-width 0px on all four edges, background transparent — the single exception being .c10-row at one-pane width, where round 3's .c10.is-mode1 override (0,3,0) had been added specifically to out-specify the reset. What the reset was silently suppressing, beyond the three findings below: .c10-thead is authored `padding: 4px 10px` to line its column labels up with .c10-row's `padding: 5px 10px`, so with the row padding eaten the SETTING/VALUE/STATE headers sat 10px right of the column they name; .c10-vrow lost its border-bottom, so the 828-row compendium had no row hairlines at all and .c10-vhead sat 16px off its own columns; .c10-att-row, .c10-mgr-row, .c10-check, .c10-src and .c10-btn lost border + border-radius + surface-elevated background, so cards and buttons rendered as flat text; .c10-recent-row and .c10-res lost their separators. All of that is restored by the one-line change.

fixes.f1_wide_width_composes_instead_of_desert: MAJOR. At 2200/2500 the content column stayed capped while the pane grew, so the composition was a rail pinned far left plus an island. Measured before (friendly-dark-2500-home, live boxes): COMMAND INDEX rail 72-340 (268px), content pane 340-2500 (2160px), .c10-home 910-1930 (1020px) -> 570.0px of empty band on EACH side of the only content on screen. Fix, in three moves. (a) The concept script now stamps `is-wide` at stage >= 1560 and `is-ultra` at stage >= 2000 (real stage width, so the shell's icon rail is already discounted) alongside the existing is-mode1/2/3 + is-tight ladder. (b) The panes take part of the width: .c10-pane-index min-width 296, .c10-pane-cat 340/380, .c10-mgr-nav 290/320. (c) Every content column's cap rises in two steps AND the two surfaces that are lists-of-lists recompose into two columns: .c10-home becomes a 2-col grid (masthead/search/banner span both; Needs attention + Utilities left, Recent changes right) capped 1400/1840; the domain overview's manager and section card lists get a .c10-ovlist wrapper that goes 2-up (new wrapper emitted by catOverviewPane); .c10-ov 1180/1480; .c10-rows 1480/1720; the compendium's facets/head/list 1640/1960; .c10-mgr-main-inner 1120/1320 with the Q/A definition list pairing up 2-across at ultra so an answer never runs past ~55 characters. Measured after (all live getBoundingClientRect over file://): 1700 home — index 72-368, pane 368-1700, .c10-home 368-1700 = the full pane, dead band 0.0px. 2200 home — pane 368-2200, home 368-2200, dead band 0.0px. 2500 home — pane 368-2500 (2132px), home 514-2354 (1840px), band 146.0px per side (6.9% of the pane, symmetric) and the space is spent on a genuine second column rather than left blank. Same sweep on the other wide routes at 2500: dest/ai overview 884-2364 in pane 748-2500 (136.0px per side, section cards 2-up), dest/ai/accounts rows 890-2358 in 748-2500 (16.0px), manager m.providers inner 1124-2444 in main 1088-2480 (36.0px, Needs-attention Q/A 2-up), all 1960px list in a 2132px pane (86.0px), copy 390-2500 = full pane (0.0px). Verified visually at 1700/2200/2500 on friendly-dark and retro-light, and 2200 glass-dark for the compendium.
fixes.f2_one_left_text_margin_at_760: MAJOR. At 760 the SECTIONS / MANAGERS / OBJECTS / All-Settings row lists hung outside the page's own left text margin and butted against the icon rail. Measured before (friendly-dark-760-dest-ai): .c10-item title x = 36.0, which is exactly the pane's left edge and 0.0px clear of the icon rail, while the pane title measured 50.0 and the SECTIONS label text 52.0 — a 16px overhang. Cause: .c10-item's authored `padding: 7px 10px 7px 16px` was one of the declarations the reset ate. Fix: the :where() reset restores it, .c10-item's padding is retuned to `7px 9px 7px 15px` so 15 + its 1px transparent border lands on exactly 16 (the border used to add a stray pixel), .c10-ix-item likewise 6px 7px, .c10-pane-head moves 14 -> 16, and .c10-rows drops from `0 14px` to `0 6px` so 6 + .c10-row's own 10px padding also lands on 16 (the row's hover band still bleeds 6px past the margin, which is the intent). Measured after, one margin everywhere: friendly-dark-760-dest-ai pane title 52.0, SECTIONS/MANAGERS/KEY SETTINGS label text 52.0, every .c10-item title 52.0, every .c10-row name 52.0. Same at basic-dark-760-manager (52.0 across OBJECTS label, object names, the AI Providers h1 and the manager body — the one-pane manager body's padding-inline is now 16 to match the roster above it), glass-light-760 (52.0), basic-dark-900 (88.0 = 72 rail + 16), and at 1280 in all three panes (369.5 / 669.5 columns, pane title == label text == row name).
fixes.f3_sections_list_row_separation: MAJOR. On the domain page the SECTIONS list read as one undifferentiated block: the gap from a section title to its own description equalled the gap to the next section. Measured before (friendly-dark-1280-dest-ai, live boxes): .c10-mgr-row computed padding 0px on all four edges, border-width 0px, background rgba(0,0,0,0); title bottom 341.6 -> its own description top 341.6 = 0.0px, description bottom 355.6 -> next row's title top 361.6 = 6.0px. Proximity carried almost no signal, and there was no card edge to carry it instead. Same root cause as finding 2 — .c10-mgr-row's authored `padding: 8px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border-light); border-radius; background: var(--surface-elevated)` was suppressed wholesale. Measured after (same screen): computed padding 8px 10px, border-bottom 1px solid, background surface-elevated; title -> own description 0.0px, description -> next row's title 24.0px, i.e. the row's own two lines are 24x closer to each other than to the neighbouring row, and each row additionally carries a border and a fill. Verified on friendly-dark, glass-light and retro-light at 1280 and on friendly-dark at 2200 (where the same cards sit 2-up). Collateral, same fix: the KEY SETTINGS table's column headers now sit exactly over their columns — thead first cell 900.0 vs row name 900.0 and thead third cell 2236.0 vs row state 2236.0 at 2500, 669.5/669.5 and 1152.0/1152.0 at 1280 (they were 10px apart, the width of the suppressed .c10-row padding).
fixes.f4_one_pane_roster_binds_name_to_status: MAJOR. At 760 a manager OBJECTS row is the full window width, so with .c10-item's grid at `1fr auto 14px` the provider name sat at the far left and its status flush right with nothing between them. Measured before (basic-dark-760-manager/m.providers): the name cell stretched 36.0-695.1 while the word 'Claude' is only 46.3px wide, and the status cell started at 703.1 — 620.8px of empty space inside one row, no divider, no leader, no banding. Fix (one-pane only, so the multi-pane rosters are untouched): .c10.is-mode1 .c10-item switches to `minmax(0,auto) minmax(0,1fr) 14px` with a 12px column gap, so the name column shrinks to its content and the status sits immediately beside the thing it describes; the meta cell is left-aligned, uncapped, and still wraps rather than ellipsizing (the 2026-08-20 'Signed in, cannot invoke' finding stays honoured); and every row carries `box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 var(--border-light)` — an inset rule rather than a border so it cannot fight .c10-item.is-active's border-color. Measured after: name 53.0-99.3, status 111.3-146.2 — a 12.0px gap instead of 620.8px, i.e. 52x tighter, with a hairline binding the whole row. Verified on basic-dark-760, friendly-dark-760, glass-light-760 and basic-dark-900.
fixes.f5_glass_search_overlay_occludes: Found while verifying finding 1 at wide widths, fixed in the same pass. On the glass faces --surface-elevated is ~0.73 alpha, and .c10-drop — the concept's only true OVERLAY, the search result list that floats over Home — inherited it, so at glass-light-2500 the NEEDS ATTENTION rows and their Open pills read straight through the result list, text over text. The taller result rows this pass restored (finding 3's root cause also gave .c10-res back its 7px 14px 8px padding and its separators) made the overlapped area bigger, so it was fixed rather than left. pm-shell reserves 'the single allowed backdrop-filter layer' for the titlebar, so the panel is made to occlude by painting the theme background under its own translucent surface instead of by blurring: `[data-theme^="glass"] .c10-drop { background-color: var(--background); background-image: linear-gradient(var(--surface-elevated), var(--surface-elevated)) }`. Inline elevated surfaces (editor drawers, roster cards) keep their translucency on purpose — they never cover anything. visual_audit_fix_round5_2026-08-21.note: Independent-audit round 5: ten confirmed findings (four MAJOR, six of them flagged as regressions introduced by the round-4 unaudited changes). All ten addressed in concept-10-command-suite.css / .js only. The headline item is that round 4's is-wide/is-ultra work was INERT in the shipped render — the auditors measured Home as byte-for-byte the same 928px column at 1700, 2200 AND 2500 — so it was diagnosed to root cause and re-fixed, then re-verified with measured numbers rather than declared.
visual_audit_fix_round5_2026-08-21.root_cause_wide_widths: render() stamped is-tight/is-wide/is-ultra onto the root from the live stage width, but the only width watcher was `new ResizeObserver(function(){ var m = computeMode(); if (m !== ui.mode) renderSoon(); })` and computeMode() has thresholds 900 / 1150 only. Crossing 1400, 1560 or 2000 therefore never re-ran render(), so the class string was never recomputed and the ~65 lines of wide CSS never matched. That is also why the harness screenshots were stale: suite-matrix boots ONCE at the first theme+width and thereafter only calls setViewport plus a hashRoute to the SAME hash, which fires no hashchange and so no re-render. Reproduced live over CDP before the fix (1280 -> 1700 -> 2200 -> 2500 all reported className 'c10 is-mode3 is-tight', .c10-home max-width 1020px / display block, attention+recent 928px wide at every width) and the converse (booted at 2500, shrunk to 1280, stuck on 'is-wide is-ultra'). Fix: the width vocabulary moved out of render() into rootClass(); a mode change still goes through render() because it restructures the pane strip, while the tight/wide/ultra steps are pure CSS and are applied in place by syncWidthClass() on every resize.

findings_fixed.1_contrast_accent_primary_light_faces: --accent-primary is a frozen-shell BRAND token calibrated for fills, and on the two pale light faces it never reached the 4.5:1 small-text bar (glass-light #8B6ED9 measured 2.79-3.34:1, friendly-light #3F9CC7 measured 2.71-3.09:1 — its ceiling on that theme's lightest surface). _shared2/pm2-tokens.css is NOT owned by this concept and was not touched. Instead a concept-scoped ink token was added: `.c10 { --c10-accent-ink: var(--accent-primary) }`, overridden to #553AA0 for glass-light and #1F6B8C for friendly-light. All 17 places this stylesheet paints the accent as TEXT or as an icon stroke (.c10-word.t-setup / .t-progress, .c10-back, .c10-more, .c10-ix-meta .is-changed, .c10-ix-num, .c10-step-n, .c10-ro-flag.is-selected, .c10-citem-kind.k-add, .c10-stagep.is-done number, .c10-qa-jump and the six accent icons) read the ink token; every FILL, border, focus outline and soft wash still reads --accent-primary, so the filled controls keep the brand colour and nothing outside .c10 changes. MEASURED from decoded PNG pixels on exact token-RGB plateaus: glass-light-1280-manager-m.providers 346 exact #553AA0 px = 6.26:1 on (234,217,237); glass-light-1280-home 'Sign in' 7.17:1 on (242,234,250); glass-light-760-dest-ai Back link 6.60:1 on (239,223,241); friendly-light 5.93:1 on #FFFFFF in all three shots. The old token RGBs now have ZERO exact pixels in those files (was 382 for #8B6ED9). Dark faces unchanged (friendly-dark ink resolves to #6FC6E8, basic-dark #64B5F6).
findings_fixed.2_3_one_pane_regrid_hit_the_sections_lis: The round-4 one-pane regrid (`.c10.is-mode1 .c10-item { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,auto) minmax(0,1fr) 14px }` + `.c10-item-meta { justify-self: start }`) was written for the manager roster's status phrases but keyed on the bare .c10-item, so it also caught the domain overview's SECTIONS list, whose meta is a bare COUNT. MEASURED at 760 after the fix (dest/ai, all faces): counts 44 / 40 / 28 right-aligned so their RIGHT edges all land on x=728 in all eight faces (left edges 715-717, the digit-width difference) where they had been ragged across a 107px span, with the open-in icon starting at x=736 in every row, i.e. an 8px gap instead of 157-300px of dead row, and no count now sits 13px after its own description's full stop. findings_fixed.4_5_wide_and_ultra_now_actually_compose: See root_cause_wide_widths. MEASURED on the live page (friendly-dark, stage = viewport minus the 72px shell rail): 1280 -> 'c10 is-mode3 is-tight', .c10-home 927px, display block, attention/recent/utilities stacked (tops 259 / 466 / 684). 1700 -> 'c10 is-mode3 is-wide', home 1332px, display grid, columns 598px 598px, attention at x=414..1012 and recent at x=1056..1654 SHARING top y=279. 2200 -> 'is-wide is-ultra', home 1832px, columns 842px 842px, and the home column now fills its pane edge to edge (l=368 r=2200, zero void). 2500 -> home 1840px, columns 846px 846px, l=514 r=2354, i.e. 146px of gutter per side instead of the 610px desert the auditors measured. Four widths, four different measurements — the old defect was that 1700/2200/2500 were identical. Same recomposition confirmed by eye in basic-dark-2500, glass-light-2500 and retro-light-2200. Both resize directions now track live at every step (2500->2200->1700->1560->1400->1280->900->760 and back), so the class can no longer be stranded either way.

scroll_integrity_fix_2026-08-21.source: scroll-integrity suite (tools/harness/run-suite.js scroll) — 2 confirmed failures for concept-10: all-resize-stale-window and all-stress-resize-stale-window
scroll_integrity_fix_2026-08-21.finding: The All Settings virtualizer computed its row window from the viewport height but repainted ONLY on scroll, so a viewport height change left the window sized for the old height and a blank strip below the last row.
scroll_integrity_fix_2026-08-21.root_cause: renderAllWindow() derives `count` from list.clientHeight (#c10VList, the scroller), and bindAllList() wired exactly one trigger for it: list.addEventListener('scroll', ...). The only other watcher in the concept is boot()'s ResizeObserver on #pmStage, and its handler re-renders solely when computeMode() (a WIDTH machine, thresholds 900/1150) reports a different pane count — a height-only resize therefore never reached the virtualizer at all. A width change masked the defect because crossing 900/1150 re-renders the whole pane strip and repaints the window as a side effect; the height-only leg is what bites.

measured_before.probe: all-resize-stale-window / all-stress-resize-stale-window, leg 'deep at 1280x560 then grow height only to 1280x1200'
measured_before.before_resize_1280x560: scrollTop 23400, 23 rows painted (ceil(227/34)+16), band coverage 1.00, bottom gap 0
measured_before.after_resize_1280x1200: scrollTop 23400, STILL 23 rows painted for an 867px band — band coverage 0.58, blank strip 365px below the last row, elementFromPoint grid 12/18 content, after 4 real resize events seen by the page
measured_before.all-resize-repaint painted-row sequence: [33, 28, 33, 33, 33] — the two height-only steps did not move the count off the 33 computed at 1280x900

scroll_integrity_fix_2026-08-21.change: concept-10-command-suite.js only. bindAllList() now also attaches a ResizeObserver to #c10VList itself (the scroll viewport) that repaints when the viewport's own clientHeight actually changes, rAF-throttled, with a lastVh guard; the observer is held in a module-level `allVpRo` and disconnected before each re-bind, because afterBodyRender() rebuilds the pane (and the element) on every render. No feedback loop is possible: the spacers and the row block are content INSIDE the scroller and cannot change its flex-sized box, and same-height notifications are dropped. renderAllWindow() keeps no last-paint memo, so the repaint recomputes `count` from the live list.clientHeight rather than replaying the stale window.
